Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement looped me in to start the sizing conversation for a Dedicated deployment we expect to reserve if the POC meets latency SLAs. High-level asks:

- Model: open-source foundation model (we're evaluating a 70B family variant)
- Target context length: up to 32k tokens (for long transcript + EHR context)
- Preferred precision: we'd like to understand cost/latency tradeoffs between FP16, int8, and int4 options
- Throughput goals: average 20 concurrent steady sessions, target P95 latency for 512-token responses < 600ms
- Security: Dedicated (isolated GPU pool) in us-west region, SOC2 evidence will be needed during procurement

Can you provide a quick capacity-ballpark and call out where KV-cache and context window size drive additional GPU needs? I attached a draft SOW to give context on timeline (Q3 start).

Elena —

Appreciate the detail and the SOW. Looping in Dev (SE) and Marissa (solutions) to validate technical numbers and produce a short capacity proposal. Quick clarifying questions so we size to the right SLA:

1) Are the 20 concurrent sessions steady during peak or bursty (e.g., 20 steady vs 100 for short bursts)?
2) Typical request lengths (prompt + generation) average tokens per request? You noted 512-token responses — what’s the median prompt size?
3) Do you expect streaming responses (we'll need to account for active token generation concurrency)?

High-level we'll consider three scenarios: FP16 (higher memory), int8 (reduced footprint, similar perf), int4 (lowest memory but may require calibration and could affect latency/quality). KV cache grows linearly with context length and is one of the main drivers for GPU memory beyond model parameters.

Action: Dev, can you draft a 1-page GPU count estimate for the three precision tiers + a suggested GPU SKU (A100 80GB vs H100 80GB vs L40s) and rough cost buckets? Marissa — can you drop in any account constraints or preferred SLA/commit timeline from the Aurelia SOW?

I'll schedule a 30-min sizing review this week once we have the draft.

Subject: Re: Dedicated footprint ask: 70B tradeoffs (32k context target)

Hi all —

I put together an initial, conservative sizing note below (numbers intentionally rounded for an early-stage procurement discussion). I attached a quick spreadsheet with the calculations.

Summary (70B model family, parameter footprint, and KV/cache impact):
- Base parameter memory (FP16): ~140 GB (70B * 2 bytes). This is the raw model weights resident in GPU memory when running with FP16.
- Int8 quantized checkpoint: ~70 GB (1 byte per parameter) — generally possible with post-training quantization; requires tuned kernels.
- Int4 quantized checkpoint: ~35 GB (0.5 byte per parameter) — aggressive, may require composite kernels and can affect generation quality for some prompts.

KV cache and context window impact (approx):
- KV cache per token (FP16 representations of key+value): depends on hidden size; rough guidance: expect 0.5–1.5 KB per token for a 70B-class model (implementation and optimizer dependent).
- For 32k context: KV cache ~= 32,000 tokens * 1 KB/token ≈ 32 GB per active inference instance. Note: this is per active stream that needs full context in GPU memory.

Putting it together (example single-instance footprints, not accounting for optimizer/overheads):
- FP16 + 32k KV: ~140 GB + 32 GB = ~172 GB
- Int8 + 32k KV: ~70 GB + 32 GB = ~102 GB
- Int4 + 32k KV: ~35 GB + 32 GB = ~67 GB

GPU mapping guidance:
- 80 GB GPUs (A100/H100/L40s) will require model sharding for FP16 70B with 32k KV. For FP16 you should assume a 2–3 GPU model-parallel footprint just to hold the weights, plus additional GPU memory to host active KV during generation.
- Int8 allows single-node 80 GB hosting of weights for some configurations, but KV cache may still push you to multi-GPU if you host multiple simultaneous streams on the same machine.

Capacity scenarios (target: 20 steady concurrent sessions, 512-token responses):
- FP16 scenario: each concurrent stream will require a sizeable slice of KV on the serving node. Conservatively assume 1 active stream per GPU pair for target latency -> ~20 * (model shards per stream) => estimate: 40 GPUs (20 pairs) using A100-80GB (model shards + KV residency).
- Int8 scenario: denser packing; estimate 16–20 GPUs (80 GB class) to meet same concurrency and latency targets, depending on batching efficiency and whether we allow modest additional CPU/GPU prefetching for KV offload.
- Int4 scenario: densest, estimate 10–12 GPUs but needs validation for quality and perf; also operational complexity goes up.

Notes and tradeoffs:
- Batching can improve GPU utilization but increases latency for single-session requests. For medical use-cases with latency bounds, batching windows must be small; gains are limited.
- KV offload (hot/cold tiers) is an option: keep recent context on GPU, older segments paged to host or NVMe; reduces GPU count but increases tail latency and system complexity.
- Cross-GPU NVLink topologies (H100 with NVLink) reduce communication overhead for model shards and KV synchronization; recommended if you're optimizing for latency at the cost of higher per-hour GPU pricing.

I'll prepare a short slide and a spreadsheet that shows per-GPU counts across precision tiers and a notional cost run-rate. Marissa, please add any procurement windows or required SOC2 artifacts that will affect timelines.

Attachment: initial_memory_estimates.csv, redwood-dedicated-sizing-notes.xlsx

Thanks — this is exactly the kind of breakdown we need. A few clarifications to help narrow the proposal:

- Concurrency: the 20 sessions are steady but we see short spikes to ~60 concurrent for up to 10 minutes after new report ingest events.
- Prompt size: median prompt ~400 tokens, typical request = prompt + 512-token generation.
- Streaming: yes, we'll use streaming in the initial integration.
- Hardware preference: Aurelia's infra team prefers H100s (NVLink) for inter-GPU latency; they're okay with higher cost if it helps meet P95 SLA.

Next step: if you can send a 1-page capacity plan showing the three precision scenarios with GPU count, notional monthly cost ranges, and any operational caveats (e.g., KV offload tradeoffs, quality risk for int4), we'll route to procurement and infra for a purchase decision.

Happy to join the sizing call if helpful.

Best,
Elena
